title: Manyhands JSON v1 stored operation
description: One operation as its store last recorded it. state and completed_step are the store's own lower_snake_case names. completed is the last state, and an operation can be completed and still be listed with a next_action: a remote synchronization whose index hand-off is pending, or a key generation that has since lost its files. A local operation that is completed with completed_step rejected was refused and changed nothing; it has no next_action, and asking for it again under the same ID begins it anew. worktree is an absolute path and is set only for a local operation; key_id only for a key-material operation. request_id, command, author, host, pid, started_at, comment_id and live say whose the operation is, and are null for an operation recorded before operations were attributed and for a key-material operation. request_id and command are the request that began it; author is the identity it committed as; host and pid are the process that last held it; started_at is when the request began it, in UTC; comment_id is the comment a comment submission publishes. live is the read's own judgment of whether that holder still works, never stored: true when it names this host and a process that exists there, or, naming no process of this host, when its indexing heartbeat is fresh; false otherwise; null when it names no host and no process. A row naming the reading process itself is judged by its heartbeat alone, since that process always exists, and one naming a process of this host that is gone is false whatever its heartbeat.
